Online:Craftable Sets:
<noinclude>{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|update=41}}{{TOCright}}[[Category:Online-Sets| Craftable Sets]]</noinclude>
'''Craftable Sets''' are [[ON:Sets|sets]] which can be crafted by players pursuing any of the equipment crafting lines: [[ON:Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]], [[ON:Clothing|Clothing]], [[ON:Jewelry Crafting|Jewelry Crafting]], and [[ON:Woodworking|Woodworking]]. Each craftable set has a [[ON:Crafting Sites|crafting site]], and those in the Alliance zones have one per Alliance. Each craftable set requires a certain number of [[ON:Traits#Research|researched]] [[ON:Traits|traits]] in an item for it to be crafted in that set. For example, to craft an axe in the [[ON:Hunding's Rage|Hunding's Rage]] set, one would need six traits researched for axes. One could also craft a Death's Wind axe which would only require two traits.

There are currently {{PAGESINCATEGORY:Online-Sets with Crafting Site(s)}} craftable sets available.

==Bonuses Progression==
Many sets have a bonus specified as a range which depends on item level and quality. These ranges are fairly linear, with the values listed in the tables below. One exception of note is that Level 50 and {{ESO Champion|10}} are identical, up to Superior quality (items will behave more or less the same apart from the enchantment levels that can be applied). The stat increase for Champion Ranks that are a multiple of 20 (with the exception of {{ESO Champion|160}}) are larger than those that aren't, so upgrading only when hitting such levels may make economical sense.

Each "Bonus Type" tends to use the same range, so any new site items you find can be assumed to use the same ranges. The ranges listed below are for crafted items.  Found set items may be found at levels between these, and will have similar values.

In Update 6 the attributes were overhauled and the values below changed significantly. These values were adjusted again in Update 15.

'''4 items''': Adds 3-129 {{ESO Weapon Damage Link|||y}} and {{ESO Spell Damage Link}}

Online:Monster Helm Sets:
<noinclude>{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|update=41}}{{TOCright}}[[Category:Online-Sets| Craftable Sets]]</noinclude>
'''Monster Helm Sets''' (commonly called "monster heads") are a subset of [[ON:Dungeon Sets|dungeon sets]] of [[ON:Armor|armor]]. As the name suggests, the design of these sets are based on various bosses found in [[ON:Group Dungeons|Group Dungeons]]. They all consist of one head piece and one shoulder piece, and come in every weight and trait (other than [[ON:Nirnhoned|Nirnhoned]]). When both pieces are worn they grant a powerful and unique ability or buff that cannot be obtained elsewhere.

The head pieces are guaranteed drops from the associated last boss of a group dungeon on [[ON:Veteran|Veteran]] difficulty, while shoulder pieces can be bought from [[ON:Pledge Masters|Pledge Masters]] for [[ON:Undaunted Keys|Undaunted Keys]]. The head pieces cannot be obtained from Normal mode dungeons. Items from these sets can also sometimes be purchased from [[ON:The Golden|The Golden]] in [[ON:Cyrodiil|Cyrodiil]] for [[ON:Gold|Gold]] or [[ON:Alliance Points|Alliance Points]].

The [[ON:Styles|style]] of Monster Helm Sets can also be applied to your character using the [[ON:Outfit System|Outfit System]], provided the appropriate [[ON:Undaunted Styles|Undaunted Style page]] has been learned.

{{Mod Note|Imperial City}}
Six monster helm sets can be found in the [[ON:Imperial City|Imperial City]]. ==Night Market Sets==
Three monster helm sets can be found in the [[Online:Night Market|Night Market]] and obtaining them will depend on what faction you align with for that season. The head pieces can be received in reward coffers for participating in the inter-faction contest, and shoulder pieces can be obtained by purchasing the associated coffer from a [[ON:Night Market Merchants|Night Market Merchant]].

Online:Dungeon Sets:
<noinclude>{{Trail|Sets}}[[Category:Online-Sets| Dungeon Sets]]</noinclude>
'''Dungeon Sets''' are [[ON:Sets|sets]] that provide players with various bonuses when items of the same set are equipped simultaneously. Items constituting dungeon sets can only be found from bosses, and sometimes chests, in their respective [[ON:Group Dungeons|Group Dungeons]]. '''All dungeon sets are bind-on-pickup''', but tradeable to your group for two hours. For dungeons with more than one version, all versions will drop the same sets. Bosses have a chance to drop a [[ON:Unique Items|unique item]] in addition to the curated set piece.

Online:Bloodlord's Embrace:
{{Mod Header|Greymoor}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{about|the antiquity|the achievement|Bloodlord's Embrace (achievement)}}{{icon|armor|Bloodlord's Embrace|al=right}}__NOTOC__
:''A long-forgotten vampiric smith forged this vile cuirass centuries ago. Though the location of his profane forge remains a mystery, this fell armor is an enduring reminder of the [[Lore:vampire|vampire]]'s dark power.''
'''Bloodlord's Embrace''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Heavy Armor|heavy]] chest armor that comes with the [[ON:Sturdy|Sturdy]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Greymoor|Greymoor Chapter]].

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': Dealing damage with a [[Online:Combat|Bash]] attack places a persistent, un-cleansable Blood Curse on an enemy. You can only have one Blood Cursed enemy at a time and dealing additional Bash damage moves the Blood Curse. When you [[Online:Block|Block]] a Blood Cursed enemy, restore {{ESO Magicka Link|1605}} to you. This effect can occur every 1 second.
</onlyinclude>
===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

|''It's not my area of expertise, I know, but it seems that there is a deliberate gap between the plating and where it would sit on the collar. Honestly, it reminds me of a drain basin. What purpose would that serve? —[[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''I just cleaned some rust out of that channel, Reginus, and it turned out to be dried blood. Finding it on bits of used armor isn't unusual, but what if it really is a drain? |''This is a strange, hybrid design. Normally an encompassing piece like this would strap under the ribcage to protect the abdomen and extend down past the legs. This does neither, offering coverage to the kidneys, hips, pelvis, and little else. —Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''There are a series of holes spanning the entire circumference of the waist, presumably for fastening. It's excessive in my opinion. This many points of contact wouldn't improve stability much and be more prone to buckling. I can't see another function. —Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''Maybe it was stitched in place? They seem about the right span for stringing a leather cord through. What about bolts or screws? We are only seeing a small piece of a bigger picture. I'm sure it'll all make sense when put together! —Amalien''

|''I don't recognize the style of this doublet. Probably a bespoke piece commissioned by a wealthy patron. The suppleness of the leather is beyond exquisite. It doesn't creak when stretching and snaps back elastically. Wearing it is like a warm hug. —Reginus Buca''
|''Touching this dredged up an unpleasant memory I'd hoped never to relive. It reminded me of the work of a [[Lore:Bosmer|Bosmer]] tanner I met in [[Lore:Valenwood|Valenwood]] who was a devoted practitioner of the [[Lore:Green Pact|Green Pact]]. The lifelike feeling makes my skin crawl. —Amalien''
|''Amalien's suspicions are correct. I've, unfortunately, had enough experience with evil [[Lore:necromancers|necromancers]] to know what [[Lore:Elf|Elf]] leather feels like. This skin isn't technically alive, but it still acts like it. It even seems to heal cuts and abrasions. —Gabrielle Benele''

|''At first blush, there was nothing exceptional about this plain, leather belt, but its appearance is deceiving. There are hollow channels beneath the surface that I can only describe as veiny and the inside of the loop is studded with teeth! —Reginus Buca''
|''I pricked my finger on one of those pointy teeth. It felt like something was sucking at the wound as I pulled away! If I was going to make a bloodsucking belt, why would I put the teeth on the inside of the band? Maybe this was an instrument of torture? —Amalien''
|''So, it definitely drinks blood. You can feel it pulse when doing so, and this seems to empower its enchantments. Unless someone volunteers to try it on, that's as much as I can discern. If I wanted a garment to drain the life out of me, I'd buy a corset. —Gabrielle Benele''

:''Canons of the [[Lore:Dark Elf|Dark Elf]] faith must learn to interpret the wisdom of the ancestors, a complex and subtle source of power. They must respect the thousands of departed of over any living soul, the weight of tradition emphasizing the many over the few.''
'''Cryptcanon Vestments''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Light Armor|light]] chest armor that comes with the [[ON:Infused|Infused]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Necrom (Chapter)|Necrom Chapter]].

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': You can no longer cast {{ESO Ultimate Link}} abilities. Instead, casting an {{ESO Ultimate Link}} ability transfers your {{ESO Ultimate Link}} resource to your living group members, divided equally among them. Gain [[Online:Minor Heroism|Minor Heroism]] while you are in combat.
</onlyinclude>
===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

Online:Dungeon Sets/Drops:
Every dungeon drops pieces associated with its [[ON:Dungeon Sets|sets]]:
* Minor bosses will drop one of: Hands, Waist, Feet, or [[ON:Unique Items|unique item]].
* Bosses will drop one of: Chest, Shoulder, Head, Legs, or unique item.
* Final bosses will drop one of: Jewelry, Weapon, Shield, or unique item.
* Miscellaneous enemies have a slight chance to drop set pieces.
* Chests have a slight chance to drop a random set piece; this chance is increased with lock difficulty and by the [[ON:Treasure Hunter (champion)|Treasure Hunter]] passive.

Items dropped in Veteran Dungeons will always be of {{ESO Quality Color|4|Epic quality}}, and items dropped in Normal Dungeons will always be of {{ESO Quality Color|3|Superior quality}}.<noinclude>[[Category:Online-Sets|Drops]]</noinclude>

Online:Trial Sets/Drops:
Every trial drops pieces associated with its [[ON:Trial Sets|sets]]:
* Non-final bosses will drop one of: Hands, Waist, Feet, Chest, Shoulder, Head, Legs.
* Final bosses will drop one of: Weapon or Shield.
* Quest reward containers (1 per week) associated with the Trial will drop one piece of Jewelry, a Weapon or Shield, but these are bound on pick-up.
* Chests have a slight chance to drop armor, increased with lock difficulty and by the [[Online:Treasure Hunter (champion)|Treasure Hunter]] passive.

Items dropped in Veteran Trials will always be of {{ESO Quality Color|4|Epic quality}}, except for Jewelry from Perfected sets, which are {{ESO Quality Color|5|Legendary quality}}. Items dropped in Normal Trials will always be of {{ESO Quality Color|3|Superior quality}}.<noinclude>[[Category:Online-Sets|Drops]]</noinclude>

'''Dov-rha Sabatons''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Heavy Armor|heavy]] pair of boots with the [[ON:Well-fitted|Well-fitted]] trait. ===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': While [[Online:Movement Speed|Sprint]]ing gain a stack of Draconic Scales every 0.5 seconds, granting you 660 [[Online:Armor|Armor]], up to 20 stacks max. Upon stopping you deal 0 [[Online:Physical Damage|Physical damage]] per stack in an 8 meter shockwave, gain a [[Online:Damage Shield|damage shield]] equal to damage dealt, and retain Draconic Scales for 10 seconds but cannot gain new stacks. * Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

Online:Esoteric Environment Greaves:
{{Mod Header|Greymoor|Necrom}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{about|the antiquity|the achievement|Esoteric Environment Greaves (achievement)}}{{icon|armor|Esoteric Environment Greaves|al=right}}__NOTOC__
:''The zeal of [[Lore:Dwemer|Dwemer]] researchers was legendary. Runes along the heel read: "Proof against magma, frost, ichor, poison, [[Lore:Aetherial Fragments|aetheric debris]], [[Lore:necromancy|necromancy]], high pressure, claudication, [[Lore:Time Magic|temporal reallocation]], and Daedric corruption.''
'''Esoteric Environment Greaves''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Heavy Armor|heavy]] leg armor that comes with the [[ON:Sturdy|Sturdy]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Necrom (Chapter)|Necrom Chapter]].

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': While you are above {{ESO Stamina Link|50%}}, reduce your direct damage taken by 50% and lose {{ESO Stamina Link|968}} whenever you take direct damage, up to once every 0.3 seconds.
</onlyinclude>
===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

| ''I understand why this came straight to my desk, clearly [[Lore:Dwemer|Dwemer]] in origin. Fairly standard construction, but the surface feels texturally quite different. I suggest one of my more experimental colleagues test its properties. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
| ''Nothing I've thrown at this will dent it. Fire, ice, poison, acid, crushing, smashing, blades ... this surface has been made safe against every test I had. I understand strong armor, but why? — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
| ''Dwemer scholars explored the length and breadth of [[Lore:Nirn|Nirn]], and well beyond. Perhaps this plating was proof against the extremes they might encounter in seeking the truths of [[Lore:Aetherius|Aetherius]]. Could have used this during a few rough expeditions myself. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-armor-Girdle-Dwemer.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Nonreactive Cincture|quality=5|antiquityid=563}} || [[ON:Graven Deep|Graven Deep]] side bosses || [[ON:Telvanni Peninsula|Telvanni Peninsula]]
| ''A belt of unusual properties. An accident in one of the storage rooms destroyed a number of relics by fire. This simple loop was covered with ash but untouched otherwise. I would have put this in the ephemera file otherwise, fascinating. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
| ''That would have been a missed opportunity. This was woven with a complex set of fibers that seemed to resist everything my students came up with to test its properties. It made for an entertaining lecture, at least. — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
| ''Dwemer, with post-diaspora techniques and an advanced fiberweave I've seen used in a scant few artifacts. The artisan's name has been lost to time but I recognize their split anvil maker's mark from other works of exceptional quality. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-armor-Greaves-Dwemer.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Thras-Crafted Breeches|quality=5|antiquityid=564}} || [[ON:Coral Aerie|Coral Aerie]] secret boss || [[ON:Telvanni Peninsula|Telvanni Peninsula]]
| ''Exhilarating. This appears to be a set of breeches crafted with materials and techniques common to the Sload of Thras. But symbology, treatment, and context all scream Dwemer. I've never seen such clear evidence of collaboration between these cultures. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
| ''I think collaboration might be a strong word. I've found some supporting [[Lore:Thras|Thrassian]] documentation to indicate contractual workings for [[Lore:mages|mages]] of great power in other cultures. Still, a unique find. — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''
| ''More than we've ever been able to prove before. The Dwemer reaching out to other regions for support in their more advanced workings is a fascinating concept. Was this a common practice, or was this more like a favor repaid to a specific artisan? — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-furnishing-Dwarven Spider Legs, Inoperative.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Tonal Pivot Joints|quality=5|antiquityid=565}} || [[ON:Forgotten Wastes|Forgotten Wastes]] group event boss || [[ON:Telvanni Peninsula|Telvanni Peninsula]]
| ''These pivot points remind me strongly of those we've seen on constructs from across traditional Dwemer regions. But they're sized for a flesh and blood wearer, perhaps part of some armor? A standout relic of their culture. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
| ''While we know the Dwemer made a variety of constructs to integrate with mortal frames, it's extremely rare to find any left behind after their departure. These joints most likely helped the wearer bear up under heavy loads, or move across uneven terrain. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
| ''They're also extremely well insulated from adverse conditions, as we've seen with several other pieces recently. Just imagine what a person wearing these greaves could endure. — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-armor-Shoulders-Spawn of Mephala 2.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Harvester-Scale Plating|quality=5|antiquityid=566}} || [[ON:Zygiite|Zygiite]] in [[ON:Gorne|Gorne]] || [[ON:Telvanni Peninsula|Telvanni Peninsula]]
| ''I've never seen this before. [[Lore:Daedra|Daedric]] scales culled and cured by what looks like Nirn techniques? What culture would cultivate a Daedra for their skin, and use them in a set of greaves? — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
| ''I believe this is originally from a [[Online:Harvester|Harvester]], you can see where the scales sat upon the [[Lore:serpent|serpent]] body. But I share your confusion, perhaps one of the lost cultures? [[Lore:Ayleid|Ayleid]]? — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
| ''You mock me when I contextualize everything through Dwemer culture but ... this was done by the Deep Elves. I've found minimal evidence for Dwemer cultivation of Daedra populations, however, so this represents an extreme outlier in Dwemeric practices. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''

:''"What Aspect will he show you? The flank of the unicorn? The skull of the wolf? Bloody claws or bloody hooves? Aye, or even the paw print of the fox? Whatever face you see, so Uraccanach says, you are blessed in the seeing." - Uraccanach the Witchman''

The '''Huntsman's Warmask''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Helmets|helmet]] that comes with the [[ON:Divines|Divines]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Seasons of the Worm Cult|Seasons of the Worm Cult: Part 2]] update.

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': Dealing damage with a [[Online:Combat|Bash]] or fully-charged [[Online:Heavy Attack|Heavy Attack]] places the Mark of Hircine on your target for 1 minute. While active, you gain [[Online:Minor Berserk|Minor Berserk]], increasing damage done by 5%, and deal 15% more damage to the target and 50% less damage to all other enemies. If the enemy dies while marked, you gain {{ESO Stamina Link|2418}} or {{ESO Magicka Link}}, based off your highest maximum resource. This effect can trigger up to every 10 seconds.

{{Mod Header|Greymoor}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{about|the antiquity|the achievement|Malacath's Band of Brutality (achievement)}}{{icon|armor|Malacath's Band of Brutality|al=right}}__NOTOC__
:''Hands that bear this heavy, iron ring instinctively curl into fists. The sound of distant drums and crashing steel fills the ears of the wearer, imbuing them with all the bitterness of Orckind and all the strength of Malacath.''
'''Malacath's Band of Brutality''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Jewelry|ring]] that comes with the [[ON:Bloodthirsty|Bloodthirsty]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Greymoor|Greymoor Chapter]].

===Bonuses===
The item grants the following bonus:
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': Increases your damage done by 16% but decreases your [[Online:Critical Damage|Critical Damage]] done by 50%.
</onlyinclude>
===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

|''Fascinating? Those rings represent vengeance, nothing more. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
|''What do you know of slights and vengeance, my esteemed colleague? Some Orcs believe the Brutal Breed had the right idea and were saddened when they were wiped out. Not me, mind you, but some among my kind. — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''

|| [[ON:Reaper's March|Reaper's March]]
|''A pouch of ritual dust associated with the cult known as Malacath's Brutal Breed. A wonder it survived. It truly is well preserved. Must have something to do with how the leather was treated. Or maybe it really contains dust from the Ashpit? — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''That's what the legends tell us. Another gift from Malacath to his most-devoted followers. Of course, they were also quite mad. Violent fanatics who swore to die for what they believed in. And they did, too. A brutal and relatively short existence. — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''
|''They would place their Brutal Bands in the dust while they slept, thinking that would charge them with energy from Malacath's domain. |''This ritual urn bears the mark of the Brutal Breed. An Orc named {{Lore Link|Borug gro-Bashnarz}} founded the cult and served as its head supplicant. Legends attribute him as the one who received the Brutal Bands from Malacath himself. Hard to believe, even for an Orc. — Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''Right. I remember that story. From the Orsinium Codex. Malacath appeared before him and gifted him with a ring for every member of the cult--after they sacrificed an entire village of Bretons to the [[Lore:Ashpit|Ashpit]]. Ghastly. — Gabrielle Benele''
|''And you're certain this urn contains the ritual oil used to anoint the Brutal Bands? It is believed that every cultist carried the oil to apply to their rings as a sort of prayer or request for perseverance in the face of endless adversity. — Reginus Buca''

|''Another amazing find! This can only be the core of one of Malacath's Brutal Bands. Notice the intricate carving, the runework. The cult claimed the rings were forged in the Ashpit and presented to them by Malacath himself. — Verita Numida''
|''As with every legend, I am sure there is a kernel of truth to the story. I've seen forgeries over the years, but only a limited number of the true rings were known to exist. This is definitely one of them. An Orc can always tell. — Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''I concur. Moreover, I would go so far as to say this is the core to the head supplicant's band itself! See that symbol? With the slash and the angle? That's a portion of Malacath's [[Lore:Nymic|true name]]! I've seen it before, trust me! — Amalien''

|''An outstanding find! See the intricacy of the twisted knots? This is clearly the upper hoop of one of Malacath's Brutal Bands! With the hoop, the core, and the loop, it forms a perfect ring. — Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''From the Malacath cult that rose to prominence after the sack of the first Orsinium? Are you sure? As I understand it, only a handful of those ever existed. And aren't they cursed as well? Perhaps we should put it back .... — Gabrielle Benele''

:''Inlaid with stolen [[Lore:Orichalcum|{{Sic|oricalch|Orichalcum|nolink=1}}]] and fashioned with very specific runewards, this belt is an answer to the dervish and daring of the [[Lore:Sword-Singers|Sword-Singers]]. If you cannot evade the blade, stand and fight.''

===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

Online:Overland Sets/Vanilla Drops:
Zones drop pieces from their [[ON:Overland Sets|sets]]:
* Delve bosses drop a waist, foot, or unique item piece.
* Overland bosses drop a head, chest, leg, weapon, or unique item piece.
* Public dungeon bosses (including champions) drop a shoulder, hand, weapon, or unique item piece.
* Chests at [[ON:World Events|World Events]], most commonly [[ON:Dark Anchors|Dark Anchors]] drop a jewelry set piece.
* Treasure chests have a chance to grant any set piece that can drop in that zone; the chance is increased by having the [[ON:Treasure Hunter (champion)|Treasure Hunter]] champion perk.
* Zone story [[ON:Quests|quest]] rewards are often part of overland sets.

Dropped items range from {{ESO Quality Color|2|Fine quality}} to {{ESO Quality Color|4|Epic quality}}, while {{ESO Quality Color|5|Legendary quality}} items must be obtained via [[ON:Crafting|improvement]] or purchased from [[ON:Adhazabi Aba-daro|Adhazabi Aba-daro]].<noinclude>[[Category:Online-Sets]]</noinclude>

{{Mod Header|Greymoor|Markarth}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{about|the antiquity|the achievement|Pearls of Ehlnofey (achievement)}}{{icon|armor|Pearls of Ehlnofey|al=right}}
:''Even in total darkness, this string of iridescent pearls glistens like sunlight on calm seas. To wear them is to know the quiet strength of the Earthbones themselves.''
'''Pearls of Ehlnofey''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Jewelry|necklace]] that comes with the [[ON:Arcane|Arcane]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Markarth (DLC)|Markarth DLC]].

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': When you attempt to use resources to cast a [[Online:Healing|healing]] ability while in combat and your dominant resource is under 50%, gain [[Online:Major Heroism|Major Heroism]] for 1.5 seconds, granting you {{ESO Ultimate Link|3}} every 1.5 seconds.
</onlyinclude>

===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

===Notes===
* This item is sometimes referred to as the "Mantle Pelagicon" style in the files.
* The Twitching Eyeball lead can only drop after defeating all mobs of this miniboss. Solely killing the Gravelight Sentry will only drop gold, whereas the lead can drop by looting the last dead Xivkyn Necromancer in the encounter.
* The Critical Chance bonus increases for every 3 lorebooks obtained, regardless of completed lore collections, unlike Mages Guild progress. There are 297 books in Shalidor's Library. The Crit Chance bonus follows the formula (1528 / 297) per lore book, but only increments every 3 books, so it increases by 15 or 16 for every 3 lorebooks found, due to Rounding. Thus the bonuses are: 15, 30, 45, 61, 76, 91, 106, 122 ... and so on.

|''I haven't seen a crest like this before. It's archaic, even by High Elf standards. The rigid, repetitive markings seem to suggest a sense of order or being part of a larger pattern. Perhaps it was worn as a boon or good luck token by the Ayleids? — [[Online:Amalien|Amalien]]''
|''It wouldn't have been worn alone. Look at the back, it's meant to be set into a larger piece. I recognize this marking, actually. It was printed on an ancient copy of the Anuad I once came across. The crest is Anu's, denoting protection and order. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''Amalien's right. Surviving battle reports from the Ayleids suggest a two-fold stance warriors could take in battle. One defensive, the other offensive. The crest is a {{sic|a|description=duplicate word}} signifier of those who prioritized defense and holding their ground in battle. — [[Online:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
|[[File:ON-icon-lead-Padomay Sigil.png|40px]]||style="white-space: nowrap;"|{{Item Link|antiquityid=732|quality=5|Padomay Sigil}}
|[[Online:Nardirin Death-Hand|Nardirin Death-Hand]] in [[Online:Tainted Leel|Tainted Leel]]||[[Online:Solstice|Solstice]]
|''Excellent condition on sigil, serpent scales individually carved. Great care was taken here. Treasured homage to Sithis? More precious than the last unbroken egg in a clutch. — Muzah-Tei''
|''Muzah-Tei speaks true, but his analysis leaves something to be desired. The sigil is incomplete, suggesting less the unbroken form of Sithis, and more the duality of Anu and Padomay. Could be Altmer in origin. — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''
|''Verita's comment got me thinking. Ayleid mythology describes a double-edged fighting form, harnessing order and chaos. This sigil is one half of a warrior's mark! Here, chaos represents recklessly striking down one's enemies on the battlefield. — [[Online:Amalien|Amalien]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
|[[File:ON-icon-minor adornment-Two-Loop Earrings.png|40px]]||style="white-space: nowrap;"|{{Item Link|antiquityid=733|quality=5|Moonstone Ring Bearing}}
|[[Online:Yenadar|Yenadar]] in [[Online:Jode's Light|Jode's Light]]||[[Online:Reaper's March|Reaper's March]]
|''This bearing is so tiny and cute! But it still spins as smoothly as if it was fashioned yesterday. It almost reminds me of the cogs in Dwemer constructs, but it's made purely of stone. Can you imagine the expertise required for such a thing? — [[Online:Amalien|Amalien]]''
|''The quality suggests Elven origin, and the material is somewhat reactive to magicka. Could it be enchanted? Or have reacted to enchantments in a larger piece? — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''
|''Jewelry isn't my strong suit, but this piece is interesting. Some ancient enchanted rings have mechanisms that allow the wearer to rotate a component, often for combat purposes. This gear would allow a mage to quickly adjust to combat mid-battle. — [[Online:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''

'''Rakkhat's Voidmantle''' is an [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Medium Armor|medium]] shoulder armor that comes with the [[ON:Divines|Divines]] trait. It was released as part of the [[ON:Seasons of the Worm Cult|Seasons of the Worm Cult: Part 1]] update.
===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': Increases your damage done with non-{{ESO Ultimate Link}} [[Online:Heavy Attack|Heavy Attack]]s and decreases your damage done with [[Online:Light Attack|Light Attack]]s by 50% each. Dealing damage with a Light Attack restores 431 {{ESO Magicka Link}} or {{ESO Stamina Link}}, depending on your equipped weapon type. This resource restore is treated as a Heavy Attack resource restore for bonuses and penalties. Your Heavy Attacks no longer restore resources.
</onlyinclude>
===Fragments===

{{Incomplete}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{icon|armor|Prowler's Talisman|al=right}}
:''A disc-shaped amulet on a chain, an engraved boot balanced on the tip of its toes and the words "Prowler's Talisman" decorate the metallic surface.''
The '''Prowler's Talisman''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Jewelry|necklace]] that comes with the [[ON:Swift|Swift]] trait. It can be obtained through [[ON:The Codex Caper|The Codex Caper]] quest and can be further upgraded through collecting gems through various means. If the mythic item is lost, it can be reacquired by speaking to [[ON:Mylen Dechery|Mylen Dechery]].

This item was released with [[ON:Season One|Season One]] during [[ON:Update 50|Update 50]]. It is the first mythic to be obtained outside the [[Online:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system.

Online:Ring of the Wild Hunt:
{{Mod Header|Greymoor}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{about|the antiquity|the achievement|Ring of the Wild Hunt (achievement)}}{{icon|armor|Ring of the Wild Hunt|al=right}}
:''Hewn from ancient stone and banded with crude metals, this [[ON:Wood Elf|Wood Elf]] ring harkens back to a crueler time. Frightful images of hunter and prey plague the wearer's dreams, but the swiftness of Y'ffre is well worth the restless nights.''
The '''Ring of the Wild Hunt''' is a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] [[ON:Jewelry|ring]] that comes with the [[ON:Swift|Swift]] trait. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Greymoor|Greymoor Chapter]].

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': Increases your [[Online:Movement Speed|movement speed]] by 15% while in combat. Increases your movement speed by 45% while out of combat.
</onlyinclude>
===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

|''Too small to be a ring. It almost looks like a ring's ring, as odd as that sounds. It seems like it's made from the same material as the other charms from the area. Does this have anything to do with the [[Lore:Wild Hunt|Wild Hunt]]? — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''

|''Yes! I've heard of Bosmer changing into fearsome waves of blood instead of animals! Wouldn't that be amazing to see? I mean … horrifying, yes. But still, what a sight! — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''

|''Can you even imagine seeing a giant tongue chasing after you? It's really too bad that the Wild Hunt leaves no survivors—not even those who willingly take part. I guess we'll have to wait until the Wood Elves feel aggrieved enough to summon up another! — Amalien''

|''I've read stories about a monster created from the Wild Hunt--one that had the body of a serpent and jaws like a shark. It's said to still exist in shallow waters around [[ON:Valenwood|Valenwood]]. Maybe it used to be a Wood Elf! — Amalien''

==Notes==
<references group="Note"/>
*To clarify the timeline presented in the ring, House Spenard [[Online:Riven King's Throne|ruled for 180 years]] before being dissolved by House Dorell, a house that did not emerge until the [[Lore:Northpoint: An Assessment|ninth century]] of the First Era.
**The Direnni's flight mentioned in the description of the Pale Order's Golden Band itself has contradictions, with [https://www.imperial-library.info/content/elder-scrolls-online-lore-answers one source] stating that they completed their withdrawal to Balfiera by the time the [[Lore:Redguards|Redguards]] arrived in Tamriel, while [[Lore:Pocket Guide to the Empire, 3rd Edition/High Rock|another source]] claims that the Direnni remained dominant in High Rock until the middle of the First Era.

Online:Rourken Steamguards:
{{Mod Header|Greymoor|Gold Road}}{{Trail|Sets}}{{Online Update|type=itemset}}{{about|the antiquity|the achievement|Rourken Steamguards (achievement)}}{{icon|armor|Rourken Steamguards|al=right}}__NOTOC__
:''Scholars believe these gauntlets were worn by the high honor guard of [[Lore:Rourken (person)|King Rourken]]. The [[Lore:Tonal Architecture|tonal magics]] contained within were derived from the mighty [[Lore:Spellbreaker|Spellbreaker]], and may have seen heavy use in the clan's war against [[Online:Arch-Mage Shalidor|Archmage Shalidor]].''
The '''Rourken Steamguards''' are a [[ON:Mythic Items|{{ESO Quality Color|m|Mythic}}]] pair of [[ON:Heavy Armor|heavy]] gloves that comes with the Maximum Health enchanment. It can be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system. It was released as part of the [[ON:Gold Road|Gold Road Chapter]].

===Bonuses===
<onlyinclude>
'''1 item''': While actively Bracing, you gain Steam Guardian for 0.5 seconds, reducing your damage taken by 90%. This effect activates only upon the start of Bracing and can occur once every 10 seconds. [[Online:Block|Block]]ing any attack while Steam Guardian is active reduces its cooldown by 5 seconds, up to once per application of the effect.
</onlyinclude>

===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].
* You are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads.
* Fragment Leads are largely found in the same zone as where the fragment is excavated, save for a few cases where it may be found in different zone.

===Fragments===
* Five fragments are required to create the item, all of which require a [[ON:Antiquity Leads#Master|master-quality Lead]] in order to [[ON:Scrying|scry]], and are classed as [[ON:Excavation#Master|master difficulty]] to [[ON:Excavation|excavate]].

|''Small rivets, eh? The [[ON:Daedra|Daedra]] do like their fasteners. I dare you to find a piece of Daedric armor that isn't blanketed in rivets, pins, and spikes. These seem special though. Ugron's the authority, but they look like they're made of voidsteel. — Amalien''
|''Aye, the smith who hammered these out used [[ON:Voidstone|voidstone]], but I don't think it's voidsteel. This looks like some kind of bespoke alloy--the sort of thing you'd only find in a Daedric realm. This sandy hue and matte finish have me stumped. — Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''Oblivion minerals are hard to categorize. Every Daedric realm operates by its own set of peculiar rules, and the materials of Princely realms often mimic their master's temperament. The composition of a Deadland ore may change by the hour! — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''

|''I must admit, the silhouette of these metal plates is quite fetching. Sleek lines, sharp corners, and simple, robust filigree. Pity that they're likely the product of some bloodthirsty [[ON:Dremora|Dremora]]'s labors. — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''
|''These plates do seem more restrained than the standard Daedric panoply. People often say that Daedra lack imagination, but I think distinctive objects like this prove they're more creative than scholars give them credit for. — Gabrielle Benele''
|''It's only because this is an item with utility. Daedra can't create anything that lacks utility. That's not hyperbole. Only creatures of Aedric origin can create objects for their own sake. If you find me a Daedric still life, I'll change my mind! — Reginus Buca''

|[[ON:Shivering Shrine|Shivering Shrine]] world boss||[[ON:The Deadlands|The Deadlands]]
|''What a curious substance. This appears to be some sort of unguent or polish. Daedra do not place great emphasis on wound care, so I'm assuming it's the latter. Even more interestingly, this smells quite pleasant. Unlike any Dremora craft I've seen before. — Reginus Buca''
|''This smells nice because it isn't the work of Dremora! Unless I miss my guess, I'd say a Golden Saint made this. An Aureal, I mean. According to my research, they compulsively polish their armor. As for why you'd find it in the Deadlands? I have no idea. — Amalien''
|''The [[ON:Mages Guild|Mages Guild]]'s surveys of [[ON:Oblivion|Oblivion]] indicate there's far more void-travel than we suspected. Dremora and [[Lore:Aureal|Aureal]] societies are both highly regimented and warlike. Given the existence of [[ON:Fargrave|Fargrave]], it's certainly possible that they engage in trade. — Gabrielle Benele''

|''Rugged. A little knobby. I'd bet this came off the back of a [[ON:Clannfear|Clannfear]]. Those beasts are far smarter than people think. I doubt they'd take kindly to someone wearing the hide of one of their own. Still, it seems to make damn fine strapping. — Ugron gro-Thumog''

| [[File:ON-icon-lead-Shadowy Creatia Stitching.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Shadowy Creatia Stitching|quality=5|antiquityid=674}} ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Aggression of Root|Aggression of Root]] in [[ON:Haldain Lumber Camp|Haldain Lumber Camp]], [[ON:West Weald|West Weald]] ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:West Weald|West Weald]]
|''This stitching is so light, so thin. Under normal circumstances I would assume it was used in creating a nobleman's wardrobe. Someone with money to spend who doesn't care about durability. But this substance seems quite magical. Amalien? — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
|''I wouldn't just call this "quite magical," but extremely magical. I believe this stitching is made from creatia, the very substance, the substrate, of the Daedric Realms. Evergloam, I'd guess, given they seem to be made from the shadows themselves. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
|''I strongly sense the chill of Evergloam, good guess Amalien. Imagine what a thief might do with a set of gloves or a mask stitched with these? The power of the Shadow Queen herself imbued into a garment. Oh my. — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-lead-Huntlands-Blessed Leather.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Huntlands-Blessed Leather|quality=5|antiquityid=675}} ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| World Bosses in [[Online:West Weald|West Weald]] ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:West Weald|West Weald]]
|''There are runes etched into the soft leather that look like others I've seen from the Hunting Grounds. I consulted Runes and Daedric Symbols by Zirpar Giralvel and discovered that these runes promise the wearer a successful hunt. — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''
|''It strikes me as odd that there would be runes for successful hunts etched into the inside of these leathers. Unless the wearer didn't want to give their intentions away, or they didn't want to show an allegiance to Hircine. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''Verita interpreted the runes too literally. When etched into armor these would help them hunt victory on the battlefield. These runes are etched in a place where they are easy to conceal. These are thieves' leathers blessed for successful heists. — Ugron gro-Thumog''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-lead-Gloamium Rivets.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Gloamium Rivets|quality=5|antiquityid=676}} ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| Shell Trove from Abyssal Geysers in [[Online:Summerset|Summerset]] ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:West Weald|West Weald]]
|''Gloamium is an odd material. It looks like ordinary silver and it melts like iron, but these rivets don't feel like either of those metals. They're cold to the touch and won't warm even after I set them down by the fire. — Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''Materials from Nocturnal's realm have strange effects here on Mundus. Darkling mana makes paint so black no light escapes from it and court fletched arrows never fly where they're aimed. It's not beyond reason to think these rivets have odd properties. — Verita Numida''
|''Verita's correct. I read a story of a watchman in Alinor who accidentally embedded a fleck of gloamium in his eye in 2E 367. The story goes that he lost sight during the day, but could see perfectly well at night . I bet these rivets do the same. — Amalien''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-lead-Penumbral Oil.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Penumbral Oil|quality=5|antiquityid=677}} ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Moongrave Fane|Moongrave Fane]] bosses ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:West Weald|West Weald]]
|''I read about an experiment conducted in Valenwood around the turn of the era to suspend a shadow in liquid. The experiment supposedly didn't succeed. I think you just discovered proof to contradicting that assumption. — Verita Numida''
|''Verita would hate this, but I spread a drop of some of this oil on a rag I use for keeping my chair in good condition. I didn't think anything would happen, but then the rag darkened. I think this oil imbues whatever it contacts with shadows. — Amalien''
|''We found several more writings about this liquid that were previously viewed as farcical. If enough of it is used, the material becomes nearly impossible to detect. I'm glad this sample is tightly sealed. — Verita Numida''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-book-Daedric Princes Lore 02.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Crowcaller's Chapbook|quality=5|antiquityid=678}} ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Plague of Crows|Plague of Crows]] in [[ON:Orcrest|Orcrest]] ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:West Weald|West Weald]]
|''The inner cover proclaims this as a book of poetry to dazzle and capture the attention of others. Given the content, I doubt the attention is amorous. Unless the author believed that guts are a suitable gift for their beloved. — Verita Numida''
|''I am not a fan of poetry. Still, I admit that the poems stole my focus. I lost an entire days work in their pages. When I finished, I found a feather tucked into the last page that I do not remember seeing there before. — Ugron gro-Thumog''
|''The poems reference knights and knaves so I think they deal with the Blackfeather Court. There's a record of an Imperial scribe going missing in 2E 219. The scribe was found several days later with a pocket full of jewels. Payment, I suppose. — Reginus Buca''
|}

[[ON:Magical Anomaly|Magical Anomalies]] || [[ON:Craglorn|Craglorn]] |''Strange; I've never encountered a Dwemer torc equipped with these shield-like extensions. This torc was created to harness tonal architecture—the Dwarven craft of using sound to shape reality itself. It was a powerful form of magic … or machinery. |''A wide [[Lore:Silk|silk]] ribbon, such as you might use for a medal. There is a faint pattern woven into the silk, showing [[Lore:bird|bird]]s in flight. It seems to be [[Lore:Ancestor Silk|ancestor silk]], but I haven't seen its like. — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
|''That's because this ribbon is an extraordinarily well preserved example of ancient silk. With the proper baths and treatments, ancestor silk can last centuries. I don't recognize the pattern, though. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''It's older than you think. In fact, this is not [[Lore:Nibenese|Nibenese]] silk at all. The bird pattern is [[Lore:Ayleid|Ayleid]], from the early [[Lore:First Era|First Era]]. Everyone knows the Heartland Elves were the first to weave ancestor silk. — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-fragment-Feathered Palladium Cradle.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Feathered Palladium Cradle|quality=5|antiquityid=570}}|| Infinite Archive chests from [[ON:Tho'at Replicanum|Tho'at Replicanum]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Treacherous Crossing|Portals of the Unknown]]. Loot from [[ON:Gw the Pilferer|Gw the Pilferer]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Boss List|Marauders]]. ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Apocrypha|Apocrypha]]
|''Here we see an example of Ayleid jewelcraft at its best. This is the mounting for a large stone, unfortunately missing. If meteoric iron was the servant of the Ayleids, palladium was their delight. — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
|''Note how the prongs intended to secure the missing stone are cleverly disguised as delicate wings. I imagine this was part of a pendant or amulet, but we have neither the base nor the jewel. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''Ah. The so-called "feathered jewels" were associated with [[Lore:House Dynar|House Dynar]], the royal line of long-lost Nenalata. I always wondered what exactly the ancient scribes meant by that turn of phrase. — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-fragment-Meteoric Iron Triquetra.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Meteoric Iron Triquetra|quality=5|antiquityid=569}}|| Infinite Archive chests from [[ON:Tho'at Replicanum|Tho'at Replicanum]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Treacherous Crossing|Portals of the Unknown]]. Loot from [[ON:Gw the Pilferer|Gw the Pilferer]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Boss List|Marauders]]. ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Apocrypha|Apocrypha]]
|''Good metal, this. The Ayleids were masters of [[Lore:Meteoric Iron|meteoric iron]] and crafted many fine blades from it. But I do not think this was part of a weapon. What is the significance of these interlocking rings? — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
|''The three-ring loop is a [[Lore:triquetra|triquetra]]. It symbolizes land, sea, and sky. This one appears to be an amulet or medallion of great age, although it's missing the central stone. — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''I've seen this triquetra before, in the ruins of [[Lore:Nenalata|Nenalata]]. It was the emblem of the royal house. This medallion might have been looted from a king's tomb when the [[Lore:Alessian Order|Alessian Order]] razed the city. — [[ON:Verita Numida|Verita Numida]]''


|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-fragment-Palladium Talon.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Palladium Talon|quality=5|antiquityid=568}}|| Infinite Archive chests from [[ON:Tho'at Replicanum|Tho'at Replicanum]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Treacherous Crossing|Portals of the Unknown]]. Loot from [[ON:Gw the Pilferer|Gw the Pilferer]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Boss List|Marauders]]. ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Apocrypha|Apocrypha]]
|''Interesting. This appears to be the hook or ring that secured an amulet to its chain. As you can see, it's shaped like an [[Lore:eagle|eagle]]'s talon. [[Lore:Altmer|Altmer]]i, I think. But I don't recognize the [[Lore:metals|metal]]. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
|''It's [[Lore:palladium|palladium]]. A rare ore much-loved by Ayleid jewelers for its luster and durability. The ancient High Elves weren't the only ones who admired birds. — [[ON:Ugron gro-Thumog|Ugron gro-Thumog]]''
|''Oh! Of course. I should have put two and two together. Yes, the Ayleids often used feather and talon motifs in their work. I'd love to see the rest of this medallion; it must have been impressive. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''

|-{{ThickLine}}
| [[File:ON-icon-misc-Welkynd Stone.png|40px]] || {{Item Link|Welkynd Jewel|quality=5|antiquityid=571}}|| Infinite Archive chests from [[ON:Tho'at Replicanum|Tho'at Replicanum]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Treacherous Crossing|Portals of the Unknown]]. Loot from [[ON:Gw the Pilferer|Gw the Pilferer]] and [[ON:Infinite Archive#Boss List|Marauders]]. ||style="white-space: nowrap;"| [[ON:Apocrypha|Apocrypha]]
|''Judging by its size and cut, this jewel was the center of a large piece such as a medallion or a crown. Its innate [[Lore:magicka|magicka]] gives it that striking color. Could it be an Ayleid [[Lore:Welkynd Stone|welkynd crystal]]? — [[ON:Reginus Buca|Reginus Buca]]''
|''A welkynd stone? How exciting! It's said that each welkynd came from a [[Lore:stars|star]] that [[Lore:Comets|fell from the sky]]. Imagine that--a piece of [[Lore:Aetherius|Aetherius]] in your hand! The Ayleids greatly prized them. — [[ON:Amalien|Amalien]]''
|''[[Lore:Meteoric Glass|Aetherial gem]]s were potent tools in the hands of a [[Lore:mages|mage]]. This one likely belonged to an [[Lore:Laloriaran Dynar|Ayleid sorcerer-king]]. I recall an ancient text that described the "blue gem" of a king of Nenalata. Could this be one such gem? — [[ON:Gabrielle Benele|Gabrielle Benele]]''
|}
